question: At maturity, _____ is a non-conductive cell composed of heavily thick-walled dead cells with lignin and high cellulose content (60%–80%), and it serves to provide structural support in plants.
solution:
The correct answer is **Sclerenchyma cell.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• About **Sclerenchyma cells** 

 
 
• Sclerenchyma cells are plant cells that provide structural support to the plant. At maturity, these cells become non-conductive and composed of heavily thick-walled dead cells with lignin and high cellulose content (60-80%).
 
• The thick walls and lignin content make sclerenchyma cells rigid and durable, providing strength and support to the plant. 
 
• These cells are often found in tissues that need additional structural support, such as in the stems, roots, and vascular tissues.
 
 
 
• ​Reproductive cell: Reproductive cells are involved in the plant's reproduction process, including the formation of seeds and spores.
 
• **Parenchyma cell**: Parenchyma cells are versatile plant cells with thin walls. They are involved in various functions, including photosynthesis, storage, and secretion.
 
• Meristematic cell: Meristematic cells are undifferentiated, actively dividing cells responsible for plant growth.
 
• They are found in regions of the plant where growth occurs, such as the tips of roots and shoots. These cells are not non-conductive.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**

There are mainly two types of plant tissues: **Meristematic Tissues and Permanent Tissues**. 

Meristematic Tissues : 

 
• ​Meristematic tissues are regions of actively dividing cells responsible for the growth of the plant. 
 
• They are **Found at the tips of roots and shoots (apical meristem), in the lateral buds (lateral meristem), and in between the xylem and phloem in stems (intercalary meristem).** **
 
• They contribute to the elongation of roots and shoots, formation of new leaves, and lateral growth of stems.

Permanent Tissues : 

 
• ​Permanent tissues are derived from meristematic tissues and have lost the ability to divide.
 
• Complex Permanent Tissues :
 
 
• Phloem: Composed of sieve tubes, companion cells, fibers, and parenchyma cells. Involved in the transport of food.
 
• Xylem: Composed of tracheids and vessels for water transport, and fibers for support. Also includes parenchyma cells.
 
 
 
• Simple Permanent Tissues:
 
 
• Sclerenchyma: Cells with heavily thickened, lignified cell walls, providing strength and rigidity to the plant. Found in mature stems, roots, and vascular tissues.
 
• Collenchyma: Cells with unevenly thickened cell walls, providing mechanical support to young plant parts like stems.
 
• Parenchyma: Cells with thin cell walls, involved in photosynthesis, storage, and secretion. Found in leaves, stems, and roots.
